findings: bm25() scans the whole match list once per statement before scoring any row (about 170 ms for a term in every note); scoring the rows themselves is cheap.

The rest of the old cost was joining every match to its chunk and note and sorting by score, path, and position. In the fixture every note has the same text, so 99,982 of 100,000 `benchmark` matches tie and the order is decided by path.

The new path scores every match in one statement, keeps the rows that beat the limit-th score, orders only the boundary tie group by path (whole when it has at most 4,096 rows, otherwise by walking notes in path order and stopping early), and reads just the winners with snippets but without bm25().

search --path-prefix public/project Proj.path: unchanged: a path prefix keeps the full query
